news.title: Ofwat consults on leakage reporting methodology
news.summary: Ofwat has opened a consultation on a proposed approach to how water companies report leakage. The consultation concerns the measurement and reporting method, not a new water tariff.

news.title: Ofgem publishes consumer market-condition findings
news.summary: Ofgem published research on affordability, trust, switching and customer experience, based on a February–March 2026 survey. The findings add current consumer context for suppliers and policy-makers.

news.title: Ofwat proposes net customer bill reduction from performance decisions
news.summary: Draft performance decisions propose a net bill reduction, with Thames Water and Yorkshire Water facing the largest underperformance payments. Final decisions are due by 15 December and will affect bills from 1 April 2027.

news.title: MHHS programme reports 50% of industry MPANs migrated
news.summary: The programme’s 14 October update marks half of industry MPANs migrated to the Market-wide Half-Hourly Settlement arrangements. Energy managers should keep checking meter and supplier readiness as migration continues.

news.title: Ofwat appoints independent monitor for South East Water
news.summary: Grant Thornton, supported by AECOM, will monitor operations, investment and the company’s improvement plan. Ofwat says South East Water will meet the monitor’s costs.

news.title: Winter gas pauses after six days of rises; later-dated contracts keep climbing
news.summary: Catalyst reported winter gas easing on 14 October after a multi-day run-up, while 2027 contracts continued higher. Its market commentary points to supply and weather risks; the published settlement figures show the near-term pause alongside gains in later seasons.

news.title: Q1 2027 power eases slightly; Summer 2027 continues higher
news.summary: Catalyst reported Q1 2027 baseload at £175.81/MWh on 14 October, down 32p on the day, while Summer 2027 reached £124.94/MWh. PEP-ICD’s separate 14 October close was £175.73/MWh and £124.77/MWh respectively.

news.title: DESNZ and Ofgem policy consultations include grid connections and supplier obligations
news.summary: A 15 October legal-policy roundup reports DESNZ plans for stronger heating-oil consumer protections and Ofgem consultations on self-build grid connections and licence changes for smaller domestic suppliers.

news.title: Energy suppliers warn of pressure from customer debt
news.summary: ScottishPower and EDF Retail say sector debt has passed £6 billion and call for a government and Ofgem debt strategy that distinguishes customers unable to pay from those unwilling to pay.

signal.label: Fix early
signal.title: Price winter renewals promptly; compare later start dates separately.
signal.detail: PEP-ICD’s 14 October close put Q1 2027 power at £175.73/MWh, up 9.7% over five days, and NBP quarter-ahead gas at 215.77p/therm, up 10.8%. Cornwall Insight’s January cap forecast is £1,999.28, £276.28 above the current £1,723 cap. Front-market prices eased on the day, so these figures are a reason to seek current quotes, not a promise that prices will keep rising.

invoice.intro: Business energy bills combine wholesale energy, networks, balancing and policy charges, tax and metering. Fixed contracts may bundle these costs into the unit and standing charges; pass-through contracts may show them separately. Rates below are included only where a published figure is available.

charges.name: Wholesale electricity
charges.whatItIs: The cost of electricity bought by the supplier on wholesale markets.
charges.onYourBill: Usually built into the unit rate; flexible contracts may show the purchasing basis separately.

charges.name: DUoS (distribution use of system)
charges.whatItIs: Regional charges for local distribution networks. Rates depend on location, voltage, time band and site capacity.
charges.onYourBill: May appear as time-band unit, fixed or capacity charges, or be bundled into the contract.

charges.name: TNUoS (transmission network use of system)
charges.period: 2026/27; prior briefing reported an average rise of about 60% from April 2026
charges.source: Energy Advice Hub; carried forward from 14 Oct 2026 briefing
charges.whatItIs: Charges for use of the national high-voltage transmission network. The previous briefing’s indicative increase is not a site-specific rate.
charges.onYourBill: May be passed through as a daily or capacity charge, or included in the contract price.

charges.name: BSUoS (balancing services)
charges.whatItIs: NESO’s charge for balancing the electricity system, recovered through fixed six-month tariffs.
charges.onYourBill: May appear as a per-kWh pass-through charge or be bundled in the unit rate.

charges.name: Renewables Obligation (RO)
charges.whatItIs: Funds eligible renewable generation through supplier certificate obligations or buy-out payments.
charges.onYourBill: Usually passed through per kWh or included in the unit rate. Eligible EII certificate holders are exempt.

charges.name: Contracts for Difference (CfD) levy
charges.source: EMR Settlement; rate carried forward from previous briefing
charges.whatItIs: Funds payments that top up eligible low-carbon generators to their agreed strike prices.
charges.onYourBill: Usually a per-kWh pass-through line, subject to reconciliation. Eligible EII certificate holders are exempt.

charges.name: Nuclear RAB levy (Sizewell C)
charges.source: EMR Settlement; rate carried forward from previous briefing
charges.whatItIs: Quarterly levy funding Sizewell C under the Regulated Asset Base model.
charges.onYourBill: May appear as a per-kWh pass-through line. Check change-in-law terms on older fixed contracts. Eligible EII certificate holders are exempt.

charges.name: Capacity Market
charges.whatItIs: Pays capacity providers to be available when the system needs electricity. Supplier costs vary with demand and the applicable settlement arrangements.
charges.onYourBill: May be passed through per kWh, often with winter peak consumption affecting site charges.

charges.name: Feed-in Tariff (FiT) levy
charges.whatItIs: Supplier-recovered costs associated with the closed small-scale Feed-in Tariff scheme.
charges.onYourBill: May be bundled into the unit rate or shown as a pass-through charge. Eligible EII certificate holders are exempt.

charges.name: EII Support Levy
charges.whatItIs: Funds the network-charge compensation scheme for eligible energy-intensive industries. Elexon publishes scheme funding information, but no single current customer £/MWh rate was verified.
charges.onYourBill: Suppliers may recover their levy costs through customer prices.

charges.name: EII exemption
charges.whatItIs: Eligible energy-intensive businesses may apply for exemptions from specified policy costs and compensation for specified network charges, subject to scheme rules.
charges.onYourBill: Give the current certificate to the supplier and check the eligible consumption and charges are treated correctly.

charges.name: Climate Change Levy (CCL)
charges.whatItIs: A tax on taxable business energy supplies. Climate Change Agreement participants may qualify for reduced rates.
charges.onYourBill: Normally charged as a separate line before VAT; check site exemptions and any eligible reduced rate.

charges.name: VAT on electricity
charges.rate: 20% standard business rate; 0% on qualifying domestic electricity supplies
charges.period: 0% from 1 Oct 2026 to 31 Mar 2027 for qualifying supplies
charges.whatItIs: VAT treatment depends on the supply and site eligibility. The temporary zero rate does not apply to all business electricity.
charges.onYourBill: Check the VAT rate applied to each site and the period of consumption.

charges.name: Metering and settlement charges
charges.whatItIs: May include meter operator, data collection, data aggregation and settlement services.
charges.onYourBill: May be a separate daily or monthly charge, or bundled into the standing charge.

charges.name: Wholesale gas
charges.whatItIs: The cost of gas bought by the supplier, commonly benchmarked to the NBP.
charges.onYourBill: Usually built into the p/kWh unit rate.

charges.name: Gas transportation (NTS and LDZ)
charges.period: Set by applicable tariffs and contract
charges.whatItIs: Charges for the national transmission system and local gas distribution networks, alongside applicable shipper and industry costs.
charges.onYourBill: May be bundled into unit and standing charges or shown separately on larger pass-through contracts.

charges.name: Green Gas Levy
charges.whatItIs: Funds the Green Gas Support Scheme through charges on licensed gas suppliers.
charges.onYourBill: Often recovered through the supplier’s standing or unit charge.

charges.name: Climate Change Levy (CCL)
charges.whatItIs: A tax on taxable business gas supplies. Climate Change Agreement participants may qualify for reduced rates.
charges.onYourBill: Normally charged as a separate line before VAT; check site exemptions and any eligible reduced rate.

charges.name: VAT on gas
charges.rate: 20% standard business rate; 5% on qualifying domestic-rate supplies
charges.whatItIs: VAT treatment depends on the supply and site eligibility. The temporary 0% electricity measure does not apply to gas.
charges.onYourBill: Check the VAT rate applied to each site and the period of consumption.

charges.name: Gas metering charges
charges.whatItIs: Charges associated with the gas meter asset and meter services.
charges.onYourBill: May appear as a daily charge or be included in the standing charge.

updates.title: Temporary 0% VAT on qualifying electricity
updates.detail: The temporary zero rate applies to qualifying domestic electricity supplies from 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2027. Check the site’s eligibility and that invoices apply the correct rate; it does not make all business electricity supplies zero-rated.

updates.title: BSUoS fixed tariff 8 is in effect
updates.detail: NESO’s final tariff for October 2026 to March 2027 is £12.49/MWh. Its fixed-tariff report is dated December 2025; no later replacement tariff was found.

updates.title: Q4 2026 nuclear RAB interim levy
updates.detail: Carry-forward from the previous briefing: the Sizewell C nuclear RAB interim levy is £3.754/MWh for Q4 2026. EII certificate holders are exempt.

updates.title: CfD interim levy rates for Q4 2026 and Q1 2027
updates.detail: Carry-forward from the previous briefing: the interim rate is £5.529/MWh for October–December 2026 and £2.979/MWh for January–March 2027. EII certificate holders are exempt.

updates.title: EII network-charge relief is 90%
updates.detail: Elexon confirms that eligible energy-intensive industries receive 90% compensation on eligible network charges from the April 2026 claim month. The levy funding the scheme does not have a single customer £/MWh rate published on the Elexon page.

updates.title: Market-wide half-hourly settlement migration
updates.detail: The MHHS programme reported 50% of industry MPANs migrated on 14 October. Review meter data, supplier readiness and any contract provisions for settlement or time-of-use changes.

briefing.summary: Elexon’s APX half-hourly index averaged £186.63/MWh in the 24 hours to 20:00 on 15 October, with a £260.04/MWh peak. NBP day-ahead closed at 207.25p/therm on 14 October; PEP-ICD says winter gas eased on the day, while Summer 2027 and Winter 2027 rose. Cornwall Insight’s latest cap forecast remains £1,999.28 for January–March 2027, compared with the current £1,723 cap. The published wholesale and cap figures support early price discovery, not a guarantee that fixing now will be cheaper.

suppliers.caveat: These descriptions are not live quotes. Confirm current rates, terms and availability with each supplier or a broker before signing.
suppliers.timing: Winter prices remain high despite a one-day pause in some front-market contracts. Request current quotes for the actual renewal date and compare winter start dates with the lower Summer 2027 curve.
